disposition_reason: Methods paper that also prints, in Table 4, total arsenic (ICP-MS) and As(III), As(V), DMA and MMA (LC-ICP-MS) concentrations in four commercial rice milks bought in local stores.

study.design: Analytical method development and validation, applied to four retail rice milk samples
study.origin: Two products from polished rice and two from brown rice (one with 4% coconut milk); production origin not stated
study.market: Local stores (city and country not stated; authors in Santa Maria and Porto Alegre, Brazil)
study.method: tAs: microwave digestion with HNO3, ICP-MS. Species: 3-fold dilution in 9.0 mmol/L (NH4)2HPO4 mobile phase, filtration, anion-exchange LC-ICP-MS
study.lod_text: LOD As(III) 0.10, DMA 0.11, MMA 0.08, As(V) 0.13 ug/L As; LOQ 0.32, 0.37, 0.25, 0.43 ug/L As (dilution included)
study.qa: Spike recovery 81-116% at 1.00 and 5.00 ug/L (Table 3); sum of species vs tAs not significantly different (t-test); standard addition agreed with external calibration; RSD <5%; no certified reference material

controls.control: Rice milling grade used for the product (brown/wholegrain vs polished rice)
controls.comparator: Polished-rice milks (products 1 and 2: tAs 29.48 and 15.33 ug/L)
controls.outcome: Brown-rice milks tAs 14.57 (with 4% coconut milk) and 46.94 ug/L (wholegrain); the authors state brown-rice milks contain more arsenic, but only the wholegrain product exceeds both polished-rice products. One product per arm, not a controlled comparison.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Brazil ANVISA (2013) maximum total arsenic in rice-based products
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 0.3 mg/kg; all four samples below it assuming 1 L = 1 kg

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Authors' iAs intake comparison (WHO 2010 figure of 2 ug/kg bw/day)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 10 ug/day for a 5 kg infant, which 1 L of rice milk could reach or exceed

unresolved: The abstract says As(V) is the main species, but in Table 4 DMA is highest in products 1 and 4 and As(III) in product 3; only product 2 is As(V)-dominant.
Country and city of purchase are not stated; Brazil is inferred from affiliations and the legislation cited.
Table 3 'found in sample' values are for 3-fold diluted solutions used in spike recovery; not recorded as findings.
Inorganic arsenic as the sum of As(III) and As(V) is not printed as a value; not computed.
